executiveSummary: GM1740's official 2025 identity, contained municipality centre, 25,781 residents, eighteen neighbourhoods, six BAG places, fifteen settlement labels, three passenger stations and six numbered-road links are coherent; neighbourhood population differs by only one resident (-0.004%) and is reconciled without rewriting source observations. One Opheusden BAG label point falls just outside the independently versioned generalized CBS boundary and must be retained as a geometry/generalization caveat, not silently snapped or suppressed. The deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Neder-Betuwe lies in dike-ring 43 between the Nederrijn and Waal, with the Linge and a managed network of watercourses, pumps and weirs. The canonical river case produces exactly 2.555619 of legacy normalized inundation stress, 13,659 affected resident-equivalents and 907,834.297 event-attributable person-hours at T+72 without selecting a Rhine/Waal boundary condition, breach location, primary-defence state, connected footprint, arrival, evacuation or dewatering path. River, pluvial, heat and wildfire maps reuse exactly the same leading neighbourhood order. The official flood-response plan instead defines core-specific pickup points and routes, while the deployed graph contains only six intermunicipal road proxies, omits local evacuation roads and both water-level-dependent ferries, and does not carry the current Waalbandijk Tiel–Ochten construction closure through the end of 2028. No acute-care department is registered inside GM1740; care depends on route-diverse travel to Ede, Tiel, Nijmegen or Arnhem. Exact service/recovery curves omit the documented water-control chain, agricultural/tree-nursery and transient exposure, rail and river-crossing state, care acceptance and accountable first-72-hour actions. Public observations and registers remain context only; Unknown and NoData must never be presented as zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1740 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK/BRT source snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1740 as Neder-Betuwe in Gelderland and reports 25,781 residents, density 430/km2, 18.0% aged 65 or older and 2,668 one-person households. The generated centre [5.5822919947701575, 51.923566734659] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Eighteen neighbourhood rows in three districts sum to 25,780 residents, one below the municipality total (-0.004%); households sum to 9,705 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 4,640. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 25,781 without altering source observations.

BAG supplies six current woonplaatsen and BRT supplies fifteen settlement labels: nine woonkernen, five buurtschappen and one deelkern. The Opheusden BAG reference point [5.631933530598959, 51.93722285813605] falls outside the independently generalized CBS boundary; the other five are contained.

Most statistic fields cover all eighteen neighbourhoods, but cars per household covers 16/18 and district heating/public charging 0/18. Null, suppression, not-applicable and published zero remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Programme Riolering en Water 2024–2028 and documented climate-stress mechanisms
evidenceSources.edition: Programma Riolering en Water Neder-Betuwe 2024–2028; Klimaatnota 2021–2025 and 2018 stress-test descriptions retained as dated planning evidence
supports: The current programme continues from the Local Adaptation Strategy and local stress tests and distinguishes water, heat and drought communication and measures. Programme decisions and planned measures are governance/design evidence, not present rainfall, water depth, sewer capacity, damage or completion state.

The municipal climate note says high river water, seepage and residential areas immediately behind dikes make Rivierenland sensitive to very sensitive across water nuisance, drought, heat and flood risk. An end-2018 stress test mapped locations sensitive to extreme precipitation; its cells are absent from the deployed simulator.

Municipal heat maps identify where long-duration heat problems arise first and highlight schools, care homes and highly paved business areas. The note also identifies crop/productive-asset loss in agriculture and horticulture and possible failure of energy, telecom, IT and main infrastructure.

The current programme and older stress-test/heat maps have different validity roles. Neither supplies incident-time sewer, groundwater, route, people-presence or recovery state; no machine-layer reuse licence or refresh cadence was identified on the reviewed documents.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Dike-ring 43 project and machine-readable water-management geography
evidenceSources.edition: Current ArcGIS REST services inspected 3 September 2026; project overview described as approximately twice-yearly update
supports: The machine-readable primary-dike project layer identifies Nederbetuwe trajectory 43-5 in dike ring DR43 and exposes project lines in RD New. The service states that its general project overview is updated approximately twice yearly; detailed project state must be obtained from the project site/team.

The water-quantity service distinguishes Neder Betuwe North, Northeast, West, South and Southeast management areas and names Opheusden/Kesteren/Ochten subareas, inlets, pumping stations and weirs. These areas show that one municipality scalar cannot represent the managed water chain.

Public map services are integration-ready context with explicit CRS, geometry and service metadata, but the project overview's displayed legacy dates/state cannot establish current defence reliability, construction condition, water level, breach, pump setting, backup or restoration.
No standard reuse licence was stated in the inspected ArcGIS service metadata. Source-specific licence/terms, layer version, retrieval time, coverage and NoData must accompany any integration.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Rampbestrijdingsplan Dijkdoorbraak en Overstroming and Crisisplan 2024–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Public Rampbestrijdingsplan Dijkdoorbraak en Overstroming v1.0, current public copy inspected 3 September 2026; Regionaal Crisisplan 2024–2027
supports: The plan applies to all fourteen VRGZ municipalities including Neder-Betuwe and supports operational response to threatened or actual dike breach/flooding. It references river, topographic height, dike-register and operational maps held by WSRL, municipalities and the regional coordination centre.

Its Neder-Betuwe evacuation appendix defines different pickup points/routes for Kesteren, Opheusden, Dodewaard, Ochten/Eldik, IJzendoorn and Echteld, using local streets and connections to N233/N320/A15. It estimates buses under explicit assumptions and lists a regional total of 76, which is plan/resource-calculation context rather than live availability.

The response plan distinguishes alerting, evacuation/vertical shelter, transport, traffic management, care and interregional coordination. Route choice and action depend on forecast lead time, inundation scenario and current infrastructure state.

The Crisisplan describes multidisciplinary roles, responsibilities and authorities. Neither plan proves that a warning, route, pickup point, bus, responder, shelter, hospital or restoration action is assigned, available or completed in the selected exercise. No blanket machine reuse licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Current Waalbandijk construction closure, core access, rail/ferries, river landscape and Dodewaard status
evidenceSources.edition: Dike-construction notice published/updated 3 February 2026; current municipal core and recreation pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The official notice says construction has started from the Tiel sluice to Ochten and the Waalbandijk on that trajectory is closed through the end of 2028. It records an active, long-valid local access restriction, not dike failure or guaranteed completion/reopening.

Municipal core descriptions place Dodewaard, Ochten, Echteld and IJzendoorn between A15 and the Waal; Kesteren and Opheusden lie between A15 and the Nederrijn. Ochten's 1995 evacuation is historic mechanism evidence, not a current emergency.

The municipality identifies three Tiel–Arnhem passenger stations and the Opheusden–Wageningen ferry. Its recreation page also identifies the seasonal Dodewaard–Druten foot/bicycle ferry and expressly makes published ferry schedules conditional on water levels.

The municipality describes Opheusden as a major avenue-tree nursery centre and the Hiensche uiterwaarden as relatively low and frequently inundated. It states that the former Dodewaard nuclear plant is shut down and in safe enclosure; current SMR work is only a feasibility study, not an operating reactor, project commitment or incident.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Road, rail, transit and external acute-care dependencies
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; RIVM questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026, CC0
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB logical graph has six cross-boundary links: three A15 relations toward Overbetuwe, Tiel and Buren; N323 across the Waal toward West Maas en Waal; and N320/N233 toward Buren. These are generalized scenario-unit proxies; same A15 corridor sections are series, not additive capacity.

ProRail places Hemmen-Dodewaard, Opheusden and Kesteren stations inside GM1740 and GTFS contains 42 stop areas. Static geometry and schedules do not establish train/bus operation, level-crossing state, passenger presence, capacity, accessibility or restoration.

RIVM assigns no acute-care department inside GM1740. Nearest straight-line reference-point records are Gelderse Vallei Ede 11.818 km, Ziekenhuis Rivierenland Tiel 12.052 km, CWZ Nijmegen 20.776 km, Radboudumc 22.133 km and Rijnstate Arnhem 23.999 km; all report 24/7 emergency care in the dated questionnaire.
Straight-line proximity and registered roles are not ambulance time, route availability, river crossing, hospital acceptance/diversion, live occupancy, staffing, generator endurance or T+72 capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water assets, grid planning, communications and education context
supports: The partial CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation contains 213 GM1740 points: eight sewer pumps, seven surface-water pumps, one wastewater-treatment point and 197 weirs. Capacity is present for seven sewer pumps and four surface pumps, absent for the treatment point and all weirs; connectivity, compatible units, settings, current operation, reserve and backup remain unavailable.

One NBNL postcode sample maps to Liander service area OS DODEWAARD 10-1i and reports queue values, requests, TenneT class 3/3 and 28 planning projects from 2030, while existing/required MW fields are null. One at-least-quarterly/monthly sample, with exact licence identifier unidentified, is not municipality coverage, live load, outage, switching, reserve or topology.

RDI returns 42 antenna installations: 23 mobile, thirteen fixed-link, one broadcast, one other-mobile and four amateur records; DUO returns 27 education-location records. Register presence does not establish coverage/backhaul/power, shelter designation, occupants, accessibility, supplies or live operation.
RDI's public WFS does not state reuse licence/cadence; DUO is a daily snapshot under CC Attribution, version unspecified. All register values remain static context with affectsSimulation=false.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat Waterinfo / KNMI / Nationaal Dataportaal Wegverkeer
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Timestamped water observations/forecasts and bounded weather/road coverage
evidenceSources.edition: Waterinfo observations retrieved 2 September 2026 18:03Z and forecasts 3 September 2026 04:29Z; KNMI/NDW snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: Two fresh Waterinfo level observations are assigned to GM1740 at the generalized boundary: Dodewaard 323 cm NAP, publisher-classed lowered water level, and Rhenen Grebbeberg 612 cm NAP, both observed 2 September 17:30Z. Point measurements are not a municipal surface, breach condition or inundation depth.

Eight assigned forecast records give Dodewaard and Rhenen Grebbeberg water levels only at requested T+1/6/12/24 horizons. Dodewaard is 326–328 cm NAP and publisher-classed lowered; there are no assigned T+48/T+72 records. Forecasts are issued guidance, not the canonical flood case or an all-clear.

No KNMI weather station or current NDW situation is assigned inside GM1740 in the reviewed deployment. This is bounded source coverage and geometry assignment, never proof of normal weather, no road disruption or safe evacuation access.

Waterinfo is generally ten-minute public measurement context and CC0 unless stated otherwise; KNMI observations are ten-minute CC BY 4.0; NDW current situations are CC0 unless stated otherwise. Every item retains observation/issue/valid/retrieval time and affectsSimulation=false until governed binding.

identity.summary: GM1740, Neder-Betuwe, Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Gelderland-Zuid agree across official and generated 2025 inputs.
notes: Feature id, bundle code/name, province, safety region and source editions agree.
The municipality centre lies inside the generalized boundary and population/reconciliation fields are coherent.
The Opheusden BAG point/generalized-boundary mismatch is retained separately as a source-generalization caveat and does not change municipality identity.

geography.summary: Administrative geometry is coherent, but Waal/Nederrijn/Linge, dikes, outer-dike land, managed water and access require mechanism-specific support.
notes: Eighteen neighbourhoods cover six cores and dispersed river, dike, nursery and polder landscapes between Waal and Nederrijn.

Administrative centroids do not encode primary-defence compartments, breach connectivity, outer-dike cells, terrain/flow, water-control areas, sewers, farms/nurseries, rail, crossings or evacuation routes.
Every local hazard/service map requires publisher, version, CRS/resolution, coverage, licence, valid time and NoData; missing cells are not zero.

demography.summary: Official resident totals reconcile within CBS publication precision, with material transient/agricultural exposure caveats.
notes: Official/generated population is 25,781, density 430/km2, age 65+ is 18.0% and one-person households number 2,668.
Neighbourhood population is 25,780 (-1, -0.004%); households are 9,705 and rounded age-65-plus rows total 4,640. The one-person difference is transparently reconciled.

Residents omit workers, pupils, care patients, tree-nursery/seasonal labour, tourists, ferry/rail/road users, responders and displaced people. Aggregate age/household fields are not individual assistance lists.

regionalDetail.summary: All eighteen neighbourhoods load, but NoData and absent event-time people/assets prevent operational exposure claims.
notes: Largest published neighbourhoods are Opheusden, Kesteren, Ochten, Kom Dodewaard met Hien and Verspreide huizen Kesteren; population alone cannot set flood, heat, fire or response priority.
Cars per household covers 16/18 and district heat/public charging 0/18. Null fields remain Unknown, never zero vehicles, heat network or charging.

Tree nurseries, schools/care, business areas, outer-dike visitors, 213 water objects, 42 antennas, 27 education records and external care are context but lack event-time occupancy, condition, capacity, backup and recovery.

settlements.summary: Six BAG places and fifteen BRT labels are represented, with one retained Opheusden point/generalized-boundary caveat.
notes: BAG covers Dodewaard, Echteld, IJzendoorn, Kesteren, Ochten and Opheusden; BRT adds five buurtschappen, one deelkern and nine woonkernen.

Opheusden's BAG label point falls outside the independently versioned CBS generalized polygon. Retain both authoritative geometries/provenance and review at display scale; do not snap, suppress or call the place foreign.
Settlement labels remain names/locations, not occupancy, evacuation zones, pickup points or service catchments.

transport.summary: Six numbered-road proxies omit official local evacuation routes, a current dike-road closure, water-level-dependent ferries and operational rail/care paths.
notes: A15, N233, N320 and N323 edges use nominal scenario units; three A15 relations are consecutive/branching series connections, not independent capacity.
The VRGZ plan's core-specific pickup points and local evacuation streets are absent, as is the Waalbandijk Tiel–Ochten closure valid through end-2028.

The Opheusden–Wageningen and seasonal Dodewaard–Druten ferries are omitted; municipal schedules are water-level dependent. Three passenger stations and 42 stops remain geometry/schedule context without operation or capacity.
No in-boundary NDW situation is never proof that A15, dike/local roads, bridges, ferries, rail or hospital routes are open.

emergencyContext.summary: Dike/breach response, evacuation, water control, agriculture, external care and lifeline actions are identified but not causally bound.
notes: Official evidence identifies dike-ring 43, Waal/Nederrijn/Linge and seepage pathways, planned evacuation pickup/routes, climate-stress locations, nurseries and external acute care.

The closed Dodewaard plant in safe enclosure and a 2026 SMR feasibility study must remain separate from an operating-reactor incident; neither supports a current radiological emergency or generation capacity.

Required T+0/6/12/24/48/72 state includes warning/forecast decision, dike and water reconnaissance, evacuation/vertical shelter, pickup/buses, route/ferry/rail control, water assets/dewatering, care acceptance, utilities, vulnerable/transient people, food/medicine/fuel and mutual aid.
Plans, registers, forecasts and long-valid construction restrictions establish context and possible actions, not assignment/completion in the chosen exercise; missing state remains Unknown.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services with finite deterministic output.
notes: The mandatory gate covers severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

Peak severity / maximum checkpoint affected resident-equivalents / T+72 event-attributable person-hours are: storm 0.658797 / 5,471 / 284,778.853; pluvial 0.521735 / 4,163 / 244,562.836; river 0.790958 / 13,659 / 907,834.297; coastal 0.050249 / 0 / 78,333.911; heat 0.596391 / 1,521 / 170,662.934.

Affected population is a modelled resident-equivalent, not observed people, casualties, evacuees, workers or patients; person-hours is cumulative weighted resident service shortfall against a matched baseline.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation and cumulative burden contracts pass.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1740 pnpm audit:model passed both tests over the complete matrix.
Service availability remains in [0,1]; hazard, demand, delivery, affected residents and burden remain finite/non-negative; repeated runs are deterministic and cumulative burden is monotone.
All eighteen neighbourhoods allocate and reconcile exactly to 25,781 residents for every service; local demand/delivery closes to municipality totals and display-layer choice does not change hazard.
Passing arithmetic does not establish flood hydraulics, rain/heat exposure, route/ferry/rail state, physical lifelines, evacuation resources or restoration calibration.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One shared neighbourhood seed overrides dike/breach, pluvial, heat, fire and target geography.
notes: River T+12–72 emits exactly 2.555619 legacy normalized inundation stress without a selected Rhine/Waal boundary, dike/breach, outer-dike/inside-dike distinction, connected footprint, arrival, duration or recession.

At T+24 river, pluvial, heat and canonical wildfire share exactly the same first six neighbourhoods: Verspreide huizen Opheusden; Pottemsestraat en Groenestraat; Echteld; Kom Dodewaard met Hien; Verspreide huizen Dodewaard-West; and Verspreide huizen Lede en Oudewaard.

A controlled hypothetical source at the Verspreide huizen Echteld-Waalbandijk centre ranks its own cell twelfth of eighteen in focused wildfire severity, behind the same generic order. This is a source-containment regression, not evidence of a real fire.

Administrative centroids and a deterministic hash cannot replace hydraulic cells/defences, extreme-rain/terrain/drainage, heat/built-form/people presence, eligible fuels/source/wind, earthquake event/site response or named cyber targets.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact services omit managed water, physical utilities, evacuation transport, external care and agricultural/transient supply dependencies.
notes: River T+24 availability is power 0.489698, water 0.421304, drainage 0.263941, gas 0.683121, telecom 0.422771, mobility 0.651337, facilities 0.469826 and supply 0.631701; no operator or authority validates these exact decimals.

The 213 HWH points and WSRL management areas do not provide complete surface-water/sewer/drinking-water connectivity, compatible capacities, controls, river/groundwater boundary, backup or dewatering state.
One Liander planning sample and 42 antenna sites cannot calibrate electricity/gas/telecom topology, live load, outage, switching, backhaul, reserve or restoration. Roads are not utility topology.
Six road links omit official pickup/local routes, ferries, rail and destination-aware external acute care; resident-only demand omits nursery/seasonal workers, visitors and vehicles.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical ledgers reconcile, but scenario selection, public evidence and accountable operational decisions remain outside the causal graph.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service contributions reconstruct availability and municipality pressure contributions reconcile exactly.
Waterinfo/KNMI/NDW, HWH, NBNL, RDI, DUO, RIVM and official plans correctly remain affectsSimulation=false; timestamped/current evidence must not silently drive a calendar-unbound exercise.
The trace does not select a defence/breach case, stress-test rainfall/heat surface, fire perimeter, cyber target, closure/ferry/rail state, hospital destination or physical service network.
Actions lack accountable authority/owner, trigger, request, decision, route, resource, prerequisite, execution, verification, expiry and rollback state.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river/compound impacts and cleared short hazards are not driven by Neder-Betuwe actions, access or resources.
notes: At T+72 river still has 2.555619 stress, 13,659 affected resident-equivalents, Facilities 0.323697 and 907,834.297 person-hours; no selected defence, evacuation, dewatering, route, care or repair sequence explains the state.

Compound reaches 14,902 affected, Telecom 0.204975, Facilities 0.315414 and 995,575.436 person-hours at T+72 while stress persists at 0.495455; no named intervention/resource justifies the trajectory.

Pluvial, winter and wildfire forcing clear with generic service recovery despite no drainage, route clearing, suppression, inspection or completion evidence. Heat/cyber residuals likewise lack operator/public-health action state.
Only confirmed actions and evidence-valid authority/operator restoration state should alter recovery; 72 hours is an operational window, not a guaranteed all-clear.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity and resident totals reconcile; one BAG/generalized-boundary caveat is retained.
findings.evidence: GM1740, Neder-Betuwe, Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Gelderland-Zuid agree. CBS reports 25,781 residents while eighteen neighbourhoods total 25,780 (-0.004%). The Opheusden BAG point falls outside the independently generalized CBS polygon.
findings.action: Retain the authoritative identity/boundary and source values, one-person reconciliation difference, field-level null semantics and both BAG/CBS geometries. Do not rewrite rounded observations, snap Opheusden or treat the reference-point mismatch as place absence.

findings.summary: The river preset presents precise sustained dike-ring impact without selecting a Neder-Betuwe breach/inundation case.

The municipality mapped extreme-rain-sensitive locations and heat hotspots, including schools, care homes and paved business sites, yet neither surface/rainfall definition nor its coverage/licence/NoData enters the simulation.
findings.action: Integrate the licensed/versioned local or regional stress-test rainfall and heat surfaces with scenario definition, CRS/resolution, building/road/facility intersection and uncertainty. Add terrain/surface flow and reviewed aggregate sewer response; uncovered cells, route passability and indoor heat remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Four unrelated hazards reuse one exact eighteen-neighbourhood ranking and ignore an explicit source.

findings.action: Replace the common hash with hazard-specific official/transparent support: hydraulics/defences, rainfall/terrain/drainage, heat/built form/presence, fire source/fuels/wind and named cyber targets. findings.summary: The wildfire preset is external-smoke dominated and selects no Neder-Betuwe local-fire mechanism.

Official context identifies riverine nature/outer-dike land and extensive agricultural/tree-nursery landscapes, but no local ignition, eligible fuel, crop/grass/reed/woodland class, moisture, wind, people presence, access, firewater or suppression is selected.
findings.action: Keep external smoke and local fire as separately named cases. Require versioned combustible land cover, source/perimeter, event-valid wind/moisture, presence ranges, access/firewater, closures and suppression; absence of a canonical local flame is not proof of zero local fire risk.

findings.summary: The road-only graph cannot execute the official core-specific flood evacuation plan or current route constraints.

The model contains only six numbered-road proxy links, omits those local streets and the two ferries, and has no active Waalbandijk Tiel–Ochten closure despite the official end-2028 restriction. Ferry schedules are explicitly water-level dependent.
findings.action: Represent typed local evacuation, pickup, A15/N233/N320/N323, bridge, ferry and rail corridors with direction, vehicle class, jurisdiction, valid closure/capacity and alternative-route semantics. Bind the current dike-road restriction only to intersecting calendar dates; missing route/ferry state remains Unknown.

Nearest dated 24/7 roles are Gelderse Vallei Ede 11.818 km and Ziekenhuis Rivierenland Tiel 12.052 km, with Nijmegen/Arnhem farther away. Ede/Tiel access uses different crossings/corridors, while straight-line distance says nothing about ambulance travel, acceptance or live capacity.
findings.action: Model privacy-safe ambulance pickup, destination choice, route alternatives, acceptance/diversion and mutual aid. Retain RIVM roles as annual static context; route, staff, beds, oxygen/power, generator fuel and T+72 throughput remain Unknown without valid operational evidence.

findings.summary: Exact eight-service percentages have no validated physical water/utility topology, transient demand or stock evidence.

findings.summary: First-72-hour impact and recovery are not driven by accountable evacuation, water, access, care or utility actions.
findings.evidence: At T+72 river still has 13,659 affected resident-equivalents and Facilities 0.323697, while compound reaches 14,902 affected and Telecom 0.204975. No ledger records warning/forecast decision, dike reconnaissance, evacuation/vertical shelter, pickup/buses, closures/ferries, water control/dewatering, care, suppression, repairs or resupply.

Only confirmed actions change trajectories; 72 hours is not an automatic all-clear.

findings.evidence: The UI can juxtapose a 2018 stress test, current 2024–2028 programme, flood-response routes, an end-2028 road restriction, 2026 Waterinfo point observations/forecasts, partial registers, a retired nuclear site/SMR study and exact synthetic T+72 output. HWH/NBNL/RDI/DUO/RIVM nulls/planning/register values remain non-operational.

corrections.summary: Implement an evidence-aware Unknown-first first-72-hour action/resource ledger.
corrections.validation: Warning/forecast decisions, dike/water reconnaissance, evacuation/vertical shelter, pickup/buses, closures/ferries, water control/dewatering, fire, ambulance/care, utilities and resupply show owner, trigger, dependencies, resources, state, valid time and uncertainty. Only confirmed actions alter trajectories.

corrections.summary: Standardize evidence class, time, licence, coverage, asset lifecycle and NoData semantics.
corrections.validation: Static plan, current restriction, timestamped observation, issued forecast, official scenario, manual action and synthetic output are visibly distinct. Absent/null data displays Unknown/NoData; the closed Dodewaard plant/SMR study is not operating generation or an incident, and normalized inundation stress is not measured metres.

residualLimitations: No expert-selected WSRL/RWS/WMCN/LIWO event supplies Rhine/Waal boundary level/datum, dike-ring 43 defence or breach, outer-dike/inside-dike footprint, depth/velocity, arrival, duration, recession and dewatering for GM1740.

The local 2018 extreme-rain and heat maps are documented planning evidence, but their machine layer, precise scenario definitions, version, CRS/resolution, licence, coverage and NoData are not integrated.

The Opheusden BAG label point/generalized-CBS boundary mismatch is an independent-source/generalization caveat; this audit does not resolve cadastral geometry and does not authorize snapping or suppression.

The 213 HWH objects and WSRL management-area service lack complete catchment connectivity, flow direction, compatible capacities, present river/groundwater boundary, settings, backup and restoration; surface water, sewer and drinking water remain separate.

Six numbered-road edges omit local VRGZ pickup/evacuation roads, bridges, three-station rail operation, ferries, traffic-control resources and destination throughput; same A15 corridor sections are not additive emergency capacity.

The Waalbandijk Tiel–Ochten closure is valid through end-2028 according to the February 2026 notice, but exact segment/direction/access exceptions and subsequent updates require refreshed authority evidence at exercise time.

Opheusden–Wageningen and Dodewaard–Druten ferry schedules are explicitly water-level dependent; static route identity cannot establish operation, vehicle class, capacity, emergency availability or T+72 restoration.

No RIVM acute department lies inside GM1740. Straight-line proximity to Ede/Tiel/Nijmegen/Arnhem does not establish ambulance time, passable route/crossing, acceptance/diversion, staffing, beds, oxygen/power, generator fuel or T+72 throughput.
One Liander planning sample and 42 RDI installations do not establish electricity/gas/telecom topology, live load, outage, radio coverage, backhaul, backup, switching, reserve or restoration.

CBS residents exclude pupils, care patients, nursery/seasonal workers, tourists, ferry/rail/road users, responders and displaced people; no privacy-safe event-time presence, assistance-needs or agricultural operational layer is integrated.

Two Waterinfo point observations and T+1/6/12/24 forecasts are current/timestamped context, not municipality surfaces or the synthetic scenario. No T+48/T+72 assigned forecast remains NoData, never zero water or safety.

The former Dodewaard plant is shut and safely enclosed according to the municipality, while the SMR activity is a feasibility study. No current public source supports an operating reactor, generation, incident, plume or emergency-resource state.

Exact hazard, affected-population, eight-service, recovery and person-hour results remain synthetic exercise outputs, not observations, forecasts, probabilities, casualties, evacuations or operator commitments until critical/high findings are corrected and reviewed.
This audit covers the first 72 hours only; dike repair, drainage, agricultural loss, infrastructure restoration, displacement, health and economic effects can last substantially longer.
provinceReviewFlags: Gelderland, Neder-Betuwe, WSRL, RWS/WMCN and VRGZ should define selectable dike-ring 43 Waal/Nederrijn/Linge, outer-dike, seepage, pluvial and dewatering cases with explicit defence/control, footprint, timing, uncertainty and NoData.

Province, municipality, VRGZ, road/rail/ferry operators and neighbouring authorities should reconcile official evacuation pickup/local routes with A15/N233/N320/N323, Waalbandijk construction, bridge/ferry/rail state and alternative destinations.

VRGZ, ambulance services and Gelderse Vallei/Ziekenhuis Rivierenland/Nijmegen/Arnhem hospitals should define privacy-safe destination-aware dispatch, acceptance/diversion, crossing alternatives and mutual-aid state.

Neder-Betuwe, WSRL and climate partners should publish/integrate the extreme-rain and heat stress-test surfaces with reusable metadata and explicitly represent schools, care, business, nursery/agricultural and transient exposure without individual profiling.

WSRL, utilities and safety partners should review aggregate water, power/gas/telecom, backup and restoration dependencies while keeping sensitive topology protected and public-register NoData explicit.

Gelderland-Zuid partners should implement one first-72-hour action/resource/evidence contract for warning, dike/water control, evacuation/shelter, access, care, utilities, fire and resupply, with Unknown/NoData never collapsed to zero or safe.
